texts.preamble: Kamal Kumar Goklani vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 26 April, 2019 1 Crr-2080-2019 The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh Crr-2080-2019 (Kamal Kumar Goklani Vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh) 1 Jabalpur, Dated : 26-04-2019
texts.facts: Also heard on I.A. No. 7575/19, an application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail. Petitioner has been convicted for an offence under Section 7(1) read with Section 16(1)(a)(i) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act,1954 and sentenced to undergo RI for 1 years with fine of Rs. 2,000/- also with default stipulation. According to case, complainant was the Food Inspector. On 18.08.1994, he was conducted an inspection in Chandrakala Sweets situated at Wright Town Jabalpur. On inspection, he found that petitioner, who was the owner of the said shop was there and sweets and namkeen were being made under his instruction. Complainant-Food Inspector had inspected the same. Thereafter, he had also inspected oil which was used for making the same, for which he had purchased 375 gm sunflower oil, after getting its receipt from the shop owner. Thereafter, sample was sent to the lab for examination, in which it is found that the said sample was below standard, therefore, he has filed a complaint under Section 20(1) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act,1954, after getting sanction from the concerned department. The learned trial Court has framed the charges for the aforesaid offences and petitioner-accused abjured his guilt. Being aggrieved, an appeal has also been preferred by the petitioner before 18th ASJ, Jabalpur, which has also been dismissed by the Appellant Judge.
texts.arguments: Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the conviction imposed by the learned trial Court as well as Appellate Court is bad in law as there is no evidence available against the petitioner. The petitioner had not manufactured the aforesaid oil, in fact he had purchased the same. There is no Kamal Kumar Goklani vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 26 April, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199795357/ 1 evidence on record to indicate that the petitioner was involved in the said offence. The evidence which has been given by the prosecution is very week and on the basis of the same petitioner can not be convicted. The learned trial court as well as Appellate Court has over looked the provision of Section 9-B and also the petitioner was deprived from his rights provided under Section 13(2) of the Act 1954. The petitioner also took the defence of Section 468 and 470 of Cr.P.C. as the complaint filed by the complainant after lapse of prescribed period but the learned Courts below did not consider the same. Apart from that petitioner is old age person, having more than 59 years of age and he is in jail since 15.04.2019. He further submits that there are fair chances to succeed in the case. Final hearing of this revision will take time. If the petitioner is not released on bail, the purpose of filing this revision will be frustrated. Therefore, the application filed on behalf of the petitioner may be allowed and the period of his remaining jail sentence may be suspended and he may be released on bail. On the other hand, the bail application is opposed by counsel for the State. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent/State opposes the prayer made by learned counsel for the petitioner.
